Investment & Plans — clarity you can plan around

Therapy is an investment in your capacity to live intentionally. Here I offer clear, tiered pathways so you decide based on time, goals, and fit. If you want help choosing, use the booking page for a complimentary intake call.

{{PRIMARY_CTA_LABEL}}

How I frame pricing

I present options that balance short-term focus with deeper, relational work. Each plan includes a clear scope, suggested cadence, and flexibility for life changes. Rates reflect my experience as a licensed clinician and the confidential, evidence-informed care I provide.

Momentum Package — 8 sessions

$1,200 — $1,600

Recommended for focused goals: transitions, acute anxiety, targeted skill building. Weekly sessions for two months plus a planning session.

Average per session $150–$200. Sliding scale considered for limited slots.

Foundations Plan — 16 sessions

$2,800 — $3,600

For deeper relational patterns, trauma-informed processing, or when you want sustained change. Biweekly or weekly cadence available.

Average per session $175–$225. Includes periodic progress check-ins.

Pulse Sessions — single visits

$160 — $220 / session

Drop-in sessions for recalibration, coping with an acute stressor, or when you need a focused touchpoint without committing to a package.

Packages can be combined. Insurance not accepted, but I provide superbills on request.

Payment & practicals

I accept card and bank transfer. If cost is a barrier, we can discuss limited sliding-scale availability during our first contact. Many clients find that a short package helps maintain momentum at a predictable monthly cost.

Common concerns

What if I can't commit long-term?
Short-term packages and pulse sessions are designed for flexible engagement. We define goals together and check in regularly to reassess.
Do you take insurance?
I do not bill insurance directly. I provide a superbill you may submit to your provider for possible reimbursement.
Is there a cancellation fee?
Cancellations within 48 hours may be subject to a fee; emergencies are handled with professional judgment. We review policy during intake.

Questions people often bring up before booking

Below are practical answers to help you decide if working together is a fit. If you prefer, schedule a short consult and we can cover these in conversation.

1) How do you approach therapy with trauma?
I use trauma-informed techniques that prioritize safety and pacing. We co-create a plan that includes stabilization skills first, and only move into deeper processing when you feel reasonably safe and supported.
2) Will you diagnose me?
Assessment is part of early sessions when clinically relevant. Labels can be useful for shared language, but my focus is on patterns, functioning, and practical steps rather than on a single diagnostic category.
3) Can I call between sessions?
Brief administrative messages by email or secure messaging are fine. For urgent issues, we will agree a plan during intake; in crisis you should contact emergency services or local crisis resources.
4) How long until I notice change?
Change varies. Some people feel relief in a few sessions when learning new tools; deeper shifts often require sustained attention over months. We check progress regularly and adapt the plan.
5) What are your boundaries around confidentiality?
Sessions are confidential within legal and ethical limits. Exceptions include imminent risk to self or others, suspected abuse of a minor or vulnerable adult, or court order. We review these limits together in intake.
6) Do you work with couples or families?
My primary focus is individual adult therapy. For couples or family work I will either adapt sessions and expectations or refer to a specialist when appropriate.
